verdict.description: sufficient is the expected outcome: true, and enough to decide against. falsified: a stated claim is not true of the code. insufficient: true as far as it goes, but a NAMED derivation cannot be made against it. There is no verdict for 'true, but I can think of more to say' — that is not a defect in a survey.

confirmed.description: The IDS of the claims and modules you actually checked and found to hold — the slugs shown in brackets, without the brackets. Ids, not sentences: a confirmation phrased differently each round cannot be matched to the claim it is about, so the next round cannot tell what is already settled and re-examines it instead.

findings.description: Empty when the verdict is sufficient.

blocks.description: Which derivation this gap blocks. 'none' for a FALSIFIED finding, which refutes a claim rather than reporting a gap. On an INSUFFICIENT finding it must name one of the four, because a gap blocking none of them is not a finding. relation-honest: whether a change stands where it says it stands, against this area's modules and load-bearing properties. goal-served: whether a change serves the goal and only the goal. decomposable: whether the change's cut can be stated and follows this area's module boundaries. routing-coherent: whether this area's health observations belong to one story.

cites.description: The exact property, module or composition text this is about. Never empty.

needs.description: On an INSUFFICIENT finding: what the survey would have to say for the blocked derivation to be makeable — the specific missing claim, not 'more detail'. Empty string on a falsified finding.

evidence.description: file:line references supporting it. May be empty.

claim-id.description: The id of the claim or module this finding is about — the slug shown in brackets before it, WITHOUT the brackets. Empty string only when the finding is about no single one. This is how the next round knows whether a claim you refuted was fixed or is still wrong; without it an amended claim looks like a new subject.
